### 2. AC Motor Winding

- Page: https://hindustan-electricals-winding-works.vercel.app/services/ac-motor-winding.html

- Workflow: core preparation, coil forming, phase separation with Nomex papers, lacing and tying with glass-fibre cord, thermal varnish impregnation, electrical bench testing.

### 11. Rotor Dynamic Balancing

- Page: https://hindustan-electricals-winding-works.vercel.app/services/rotor-balancing.html
- Scope: two-plane dynamic balancing of motor rotors, squirrel-cage rotors and wound armatures, plus fan, blower wheel and pulley balancing.
- Why it matters: a perfectly rewound motor still fails early if its rotor runs out of balance. Unbalance accelerates bearing wear, damages end shields, causes shaft bending and raises winding temperature.
- When required: strong motor vibration, after a bent or machined shaft, after catastrophic bearing failure, and after rewinding a high-speed or large motor.
- Workflow: vibration assessment, rotor preparation and shaft truth check, spin balancing in both correction planes, precision weight correction by adding or removing material, reassembly check at operating speed.
- CTA on page: Call +91 98252 72547 or request a WhatsApp quote.

## Equipment and Motor Type Capability Matrix

### Motors Rewound

- AC 3-phase squirrel cage induction motors - pumps, blowers, compressors, conveyors, mixers, agitators.
- AC slip ring / wound rotor motors - cranes, hoists and machinery needing high starting torque.
- AC single-phase capacitor start and run motors - utility pumps, exhaust units, workshop equipment.
- AC multi-speed and dual-speed motors - Dahlander winding and dual separate winding configurations.
- DC series, shunt and compound motors - including armatures, interpoles and field coils.
- Submersible pump motors - borewell, sump and dewatering units.
- Industrial blower and fan motors - ID fan, FD fan, exhaust fan, roof fan, centrifugal blower.
- Generator and alternator stators, exciter rotors and field windings.
- Transformer coils - control, step-down, isolation, rectifier and welding transformers.
- Welding machine transformer coils - ARC, MIG and TIG units, oil-cooled and air-cooled.

### Mechanical Work Performed Alongside Rewinding

- Precision bearing replacement with C3 clearance industrial grade bearings, hydraulic press fitment.
- Rotor shaft truing, machining and sleeving; shaft run-out measurement with a dial gauge.
- Bearing housing boring and sleeving to correct ovality.
- Commutator turning, segment chamfering and mica undercutting.
- Brush gear and brush housing servicing, brush bedding and neutral axis setting.
- Two-plane dynamic rotor balancing, fan wheel and pulley balancing.
- End shield bushing replacement, cooling fan and impeller replacement.
- Terminal block replacement with porcelain or Bakelite blocks and silicone sealing, plus heat-resistant lead wire.

### Electrical Work Performed Alongside Rewinding

- Megger insulation resistance testing at 500V and 1000V.
- Digital micro-ohm phase resistance balance measurement.
- High-potential and surge testing.
- Growler testing of armature cores with a feeler blade to pinpoint shorted turns.
- No-load run testing and 3-phase current balance measurement.
- Excitation circuit checks for residual magnetism, AVR wiring and rectifier diodes.
- Open-circuit voltage ratio and short-circuit current testing for transformers.
- Load and arc strike testing for welding machines.

## Service Intake and Workflow Summary

1. Inquiry - call +91 98252 72547 or WhatsApp the same number with nameplate details and the observed fault.
2. Preliminary estimate - budgetary figure based on customer-supplied information; explicitly non-binding.
3. Motor dispatch - customer transports the motor to Shop No. 28 and 29, Express House, GIDC Vapi, using N.H. 48 highway access, unless logistics are mutually arranged.
4. Inspection - Megger insulation test, resistance measurement, surge test, bearing check, shaft run-out check and visual core and slot inspection.
5. Winding data logging - original wire gauge, slot turns, coil span, connection scheme, lap or wave winding, slot pitch, equalizer connections and commutator riser pitch recorded before stripping.
6. Fault cause determination - external causes such as single phasing, overloading, moisture or blocked cooling identified and reported alongside the winding fault.
7. Final quotation - issued after physical inspection, Megger testing and, where required, disassembly.
8. Rework approval - hidden mechanical defects such as cracked rotor bars, bent shafts or damaged bearing housings are reported and approved before extra machining or parts replacement.
9. Rewind, impregnate and bake - precision coil winding, varnish impregnation and controlled oven baking.
10. Post-rework testing - Megger repeat, resistance balance, no-load run, phase current balance, and dynamic balancing if required.
11. Delivery or collection - repaired equipment should be collected within 30 days of completion notification.
12. Post-repair support - diagnostic guidance on supply-side issues and underlying fault causes to prevent repeat failures.

## Technical Capabilities

### Materials

- Winding wire: 100% super-enameled electrolytic grade copper wire, chosen for high conductivity and thermal performance.
- Slot and phase insulation: Class F and Class H systems using Nomex, Mylar, Kapton and Kraft insulating papers.
- Impregnation: high-grade electrical varnish applied by vacuum impregnation or dip, followed by controlled oven baking.

### Insulation Classes

- Class F: maximum winding operating temperature 155 degrees C at the hottest spot.
- Class H: maximum winding operating temperature 180 degrees C at the hottest spot.
- Class H is selected for continuous heavy load duty, hot or poorly ventilated locations, and positions close to furnaces and boilers.
- Class selection follows the motor's original nameplate and its real working environment.

### Testing Performed

- Pre-rewinding: 1000V Megger insulation resistance test, phase resistance balance using a digital micro-ohm meter, visual core and slot inspection, surge testing.
- Post-rewinding: repeated Megger test, winding resistance balance across all phases, no-load run test, 3-phase current balance check, high-potential insulation test.
- Mechanical: shaft run-out check with a dial gauge, bearing housing bore ovality inspection, armature growler testing, dynamic rotor balancing in two planes.
- Winding data recorded before stripping: wire gauge, slot turns, coil span, connection scheme, lap or wave winding scheme, slot pitch, equalizer connections and commutator riser pitch.

### Workshop Principles

- Fault cause is diagnosed before rewinding, because rewinding without correcting the underlying fault only burns the next winding.
- Original factory winding data is recorded and followed so the rebuilt unit restores full operational torque and efficiency.
- Hidden mechanical defects found during dismantling are reported to the customer and approved before extra machining or parts replacement.

## Five-Step Rewinding Process

1. Inspection - Megger insulation test, surge test, bearing check and root cause fault identification.
2. Dismantling - careful core disassembly, coil burnout data logging and slot cleaning without warping stator laminations.
3. Precision Rewinding - exact turn counts wound with super-enameled electrolytic copper wire and Class F/H slot insulation.
4. Varnishing and Curing - deep varnish impregnation and controlled oven baking to eliminate moisture and vibration.
5. Testing and Delivery - no-load current testing, resistance balance, phase current balance and final quality sign-off.

## Diagnostic Signals and Workshop Answers

- Symptom: abnormal overheating, breaker or overload relay tripping, burnt or smoky smell, low insulation resistance, unsteady speed or phase current imbalance. Answer: these are the standard warning signs of a failed motor winding. Bring the motor to the workshop for a winding and insulation test.
- Symptom: motor keeps burning out even after rewinding. Answer: the cause is usually external, such as unbalanced supply voltage, overloading, single phasing, low voltage, moisture ingress or blocked cooling.
- Symptom: 3-phase motor trips on overload. Answer: never increase the overload relay setting above nameplate current without finding the cause. Common causes are mechanical overload, low or unbalanced supply voltage, a partially open phase, shorted turns, or a seized load.
- Symptom: one supply line is lost. Answer: single phasing happens from a blown fuse, loose connection, faulty contactor pole or broken cable. Running on two phases can burn the winding within minutes if protection does not trip.
- Symptom: loud noise and vibration. Answer: most often worn or seized bearings, rotor unbalance, shaft misalignment, a broken cooling fan rubbing the end cover, or loose motor mountings.
- Symptom: bearing play when the shaft is rocked by hand, rumbling noise that rises with speed, extra heat near the end covers. Answer: bearings need replacement. Ignored, the rotor rubs the stator core and causes a costly winding burnout.
- Symptom: Megger reading near zero or falling as the test runs. Answer: this almost always means moisture ingress or burnt insulation. The winding must not be energized until repaired.
- Symptom: submersible pump trips after running for some time. Answer: usually moisture ingress through a damaged cable joint or worn mechanical seal, silt locking the impeller, a hot-sensitive winding fault, or dry running from low water level.
- Symptom: welding unit gives a weak arc strike, excessive hum, erratic current control or coil burnout. Answer: secondary copper strips, current selector switches, core clamping or internal insulation are the usual failure points.
- Symptom: generator produces zero output voltage or fluctuating voltage under load. Answer: excitation circuit, AVR wiring and rectifier diodes are checked before assuming winding failure.
- Symptom: transformer gives incorrect secondary voltage, electrical noise or ground loops. Answer: lamination core condition, turns-per-volt accuracy and inter-winding shielding are checked during assessment.
- Question: is on-site diagnosis available? Answer: rewinding, varnish baking, bearing replacement and rotor balancing require dedicated bench tools, ovens and test equipment, so most work is done at the workshop. Initial supply-side and tripping issues can be guided over the phone.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What motor rewinding and repair services do you provide in Vapi?

AC single-phase and 3-phase induction motors, DC motors, industrial generators and alternators, transformers and welding machines, plus pump motor rewinding, submersible pump repair, blower motor winding and rotor balancing, all from the GIDC Vapi workshop.

### How much does motor rewinding cost?

Cost depends mainly on the motor's HP/kW rating and frame size, the copper quantity, the insulation class used, and whether additional mechanical work such as shaft or bearing repair is required. There is no fixed price. The motor is inspected first and an estimate is given before work starts.

### How long does motor rewinding take?

Turnaround depends on motor size, winding complexity, core condition and current workshop workload. Emergency breakdowns for manufacturing plants in Vapi GIDC and nearby industrial belts are prioritised. Call with the motor details for a realistic timeline.

### Should the motor be rewound or replaced?

For large industrial and non-standard motors that are hard to source, rewinding is usually far more economical. For small standard motors that are cheap to replace, replacement may make more sense. The recommendation is given honestly after inspection.

### What copper wire and insulation do you use?

100% super-enameled electrolytic grade copper wire with high-temperature Class F and Class H insulating papers and varnishes, matched to the motor's operating conditions.

### Do you rewind AC induction motors?

Yes, single-phase and 3-phase AC induction motors including squirrel cage and slip ring types, with phase-to-phase insulation, slot insulation and balanced winding.

### Do you handle DC motor winding and repair?

Yes, armature rewinding, field coil repair, commutator turning, mica undercutting, and brush and brush-housing servicing for variable speed drives, cranes and machine tools.

### Can you repair pump, submersible and blower motors?

Yes, centrifugal and chemical pump motors, borewell and dewatering submersible motor windings, and ID/FD fan, exhaust and centrifugal blower motors, including insulation testing and rotor balancing.

### Do you repair generators and alternators?

Yes, main stators, exciter rotors, field windings and faulty diode assemblies, followed by electrical testing before delivery.

### Do you provide transformer rewinding?

Yes, control transformers, step-down transformers and industrial welding transformers using quality copper wire and proper dielectric insulation, with insulation testing after completion.

### What testing is performed before and after rewinding?

Before: 1000V Megger insulation resistance, digital micro-ohm phase resistance balance, and visual core-and-slot inspection. After: Megger repeat, resistance balance across all phases, no-load run test, 3-phase current balance, and dynamic balancing where rotor vibration is suspected.

### What is a Megger test?

A Megger is an insulation resistance tester applying 500V or 1000V DC between winding conductors and the motor frame. A healthy industrial motor shows several megaohms and a stable reading. Below 1 megaohm on a 400V class motor is a warning; near zero or a continuously falling reading means moisture ingress or burnt insulation.

### What is the difference between Class F and Class H insulation?

Insulation class defines the maximum allowable winding operating temperature. Class F is rated 155 degrees C and Class H 180 degrees C at the hottest spot. Class H suits continuous heavy load, hot or poorly ventilated areas, and locations near furnaces and boilers.

### What information is needed for a repair estimate?

Manufacturer, HP or kW rating, voltage, number of phases, RPM or speed, frame size if visible, insulation class, the exact fault being observed, approximate motor age, installation location, and photos of the nameplate and motor condition sent on WhatsApp.

### Can a rewound motor match a new motor?

Yes, when the original winding data is followed, genuine electrolytic-grade copper wire is used, slot and phase insulation is correct, and impregnation and curing are properly done. The result matches or exceeds original factory specifications.

### How important is shaft and bearing housing repair?

Extremely important. A worn shaft journal or loose end-cover bearing housing makes even a new bearing run eccentric, causing heavy vibration and destroying the bearing within weeks. Skipping these checks is the single most common reason a good rewinding job fails prematurely.

### Do you handle emergency breakdown jobs for factories in GIDC Vapi?

Yes. Emergency breakdowns for manufacturing plants, chemical units, paper mills and packaging lines in GIDC Vapi and nearby belts get priority scheduling. Call +91 98252 72547 with the motor rating and which machine is down.

### Where is the workshop and which areas are served?

Shop No. 28 & 29, Express House, Near C.N.G. Gujarat Gas Station, N.H. 48, GIDC, Vapi, Gujarat 396195, with direct highway access for motor loading and unloading. Service covers GIDC Vapi, Silvassa, Daman, Valsad, Pardi, Bhilad and Sarigam GIDC.

### How do I request a quote?

Call +91 98252 72547 or message the same number on WhatsApp with nameplate details and the fault being seen. A quote form is also available on the contact page.

## Industries Served

- Chemical plants - corrosion-resistant Class H winding for chemical agitator and pump motors.
- Textile and dyeing - continuous duty blower, stenter and loom motor rewinding.
- Packaging and paper - drive motors, paper mill pulper drives and corrugation line motors.
- Engineering and plastics - hydraulic pump motors, extruders, granulators and machine tool spindles.
- Manufacturing - general continuous duty drive motors and production machinery.
- Power generation - standby and continuous diesel generator sets and alternators.
- Fabrication workshops - ARC, MIG and TIG welding machines and welding transformers.
- Water and utilities - borewell submersibles, dewatering pumps, transfer and process pumps.
- HVAC and process ventilation - ID fans, FD fans, exhaust fans, roof fans and centrifugal blowers.

## Service Areas

- Vapi and GIDC Vapi - workshop base at Shop 28 and 29, Express House, near the CNG Gas Station on N.H. 48. Fast repair turnaround for local chemical, paper, packaging and textile plants.
- Silvassa, Dadra and Nagar Haveli - highway dispatch for plastic injection moulding, wire drawing, packaging and heavy manufacturing units.
- Daman industrial belt - overhauling electric motors, transformers and generators for manufacturing, pharmaceutical and blow-moulding plants.
- Valsad district - rewinding and repair for industrial drive motors, commercial pumps and plant power equipment.
- Pardi - quick breakdown response for engineering workshops and agricultural and industrial pump motors.
- Bhilad and Sarigam GIDC - N.H. 48 corridor proximity for smooth transit of heavy 3-phase motors.

## Visiting the Workshop

- Landmark: Express House, immediately beside the C.N.G. Gujarat Gas Station.
- Road: National Highway 48, GIDC, Vapi.
- Shop numbers: 28 and 29.
- Loading access: direct N.H. 48 frontage allows cranes, pickups and trucks carrying heavy industrial motors to load and unload at the shop.
- Who visits: plant engineers, maintenance managers, procurement staff and workshop owners from chemical, paper, packaging, textile, engineering and plastics units.
- Walk-in inspection: factory engineers and maintenance managers are welcome to inspect the winding facility firsthand before deciding on a repair.
- Best time to visit: Monday to Saturday between 9:00 AM and 8:00 PM.
- Bring for a firm estimate: the motor itself where possible, plus nameplate photos and a clear description of the fault.
- Map: https://maps.google.com/?q=20.3631135,72.9210025

## Requesting a Quote

Information that speeds up an accurate estimate:

- Motor manufacturer and make.
- HP or kW rating and frame size.
- Voltage and number of phases.
- RPM or speed and insulation class from the nameplate.
- The exact fault observed, such as tripping immediately, running hot, making noise or not starting.
- Approximate motor age and where it is installed.
- Photos of the nameplate and general motor condition, ideally sent on WhatsApp.
